audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart is shifted by one row against its own why strings on all seven rows. Row 0's why says 'a farm standoff' but the side reads Wukong; row 2's why says 'He out-trades you' but the side reads K'Sante; row 6's why says 'Wukong reclaims it' but the side reads K'Sante.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill / Wukong / Wukong / Wukong / K'Sante / Skill / Wukong, which matches every why string exactly, and matches the 47.43% win rate over 1166 games — a Wukong-favoured lane whose one K'Sante window is level 6.
audit.corrected: All seven rows realigned to Skill / Wukong / Wukong / Wukong / K'Sante / Skill / Wukong, with ratings inverted to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes referred to 'his Q', 'his clone (W)', 'his E' and 'his R spin' without ever naming them.
audit.why: The packet flags this matchup as never naming a single Wukong ability. The real names are Stone Skin, Crushing Blow, Warrior Trickster, Nimbus Strike and Cyclone.
audit.corrected: All four spikes now name the abilities. Cooldown numbers were NOT added — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: K'Sante's 2-stack Ntofo Strikes was called 'Q3's knock-up'; it is a shockwave that pulls in. The flagged auto-attack-reset tell on Crushing Blow was absent, which matters because the clone read depends on watching the wind-up.
audit.why: Riot's Q text: 'At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in.' The missing-interactions file flags Crushing Blow as an attack reset — his combo opens on the wind-up, not the cast.
audit.corrected: Pull replaces knock-up throughout; the attack-reset tell is now stated in the early block.

edits.before: His Q armor-shreds your early trades and his clone (W) lets him bait your cooldowns before you have your full combo.
edits.after: Crushing Blow shreds your armour and Warrior Trickster's clone baits your cooldowns before your full combo exists.

edits.before: He out-trades you around your Q cooldown using E to gap-close in and out faster than your short-range W can answer.
edits.after: He out-trades around your Q using Nimbus Strike to gap-close faster than your 600-range W charge can answer.

edits.before: All Out converts you to a duelist and the R knockback survives his E-Q-W-R — bait the clone and his ult spin, then dash the real him.
edits.after: All Out makes you a duelist and your R launches him out of Cyclone — bait the clone and the spin, then dash onto the real him.

edits.before: His Q armor-shred ignores your armor stacking and his R AoE knockup out-scales your single-target peel — recall him with R instead of dueling.
edits.after: Crushing Blow's shred beats armour stacking and Cyclone's AoE knockup out-scales single-target peel — launch him with R, never duel.

edits.before: Your Q-W combo comes online — your only real trading window where you can charge W into him and land Q3's knock-up before he can E-Q-W out.
edits.after: Your Q-W comes online — the one trading window where you charge W into him and land the 2-stack Ntofo pull before he Nimbus Strikes out.

edits.before: Wukong's threat window: his clone (W) bait plus Q armor-shred and E gap-close out-trade your low-econ early, especially if he punishes your Q on cooldown.
edits.after: Wukong's threat window: Warrior Trickster's clone plus Crushing Blow's shred and Nimbus Strike's gap-close out-trade your early, worst when your Q is down.

edits.before: Wukong reclaims it: his Q armor-shred ignores your armor stacking and his R AoE knockup makes him the bigger teamfight threat — peel rather than duel.
edits.after: Wukong reclaims it: Crushing Blow's shred beats your armour stacking and Cyclone's AoE knockup makes him the bigger fight threat — peel, never duel.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash — you only have Q with no engage, and he can't commit without his E dash yet, so just farm with the tip of Q. The problem starts at 2-3: his Q shreds your armor and his clone (W) makes it hard to read which is the real Wukong before you blow your W charge. Don't throw W at a clone or burn Q3 on the decoy — if you whiff your combo into a juke he E-Q's onto you and wins the trade clean.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — you only have Q with no engage, and he cannot commit without Nimbus Strike, so farm at the tip of Q. The problem starts at 2-3: Crushing Blow shreds your armour and Warrior Trickster's clone hides which body is real before you blow the W charge. Watch his auto wind-up, not the cast — Crushing Blow is an attack reset. Never spend W or the Ntofo pull on a decoy; whiff and he lands on you clean.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still his — he trades around your Q cooldown and his E gap-close means you can't punish him on the back foot the way you do an immobile bruiser. Your spike is 6: All Out gives you a duelist profile and the R knockback can survive his full E-Q-W-R combo, so bait his ult spin and his clone first, then dash through the real Wukong while his lockdown is down. Win it here on a good R or you don't win it.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still his — he trades around your Q cooldown and Nimbus Strike's gap-close means you cannot punish him on the back foot the way you do an immobile bruiser. Your spike is 6: All Out gives you a duelist profile and R launches him out of Cyclone's spin, so bait the clone and the ultimate first, then dash onto the real Wukong while his lockdown is down. Win it here on a good R or you do not win it.

edits.before: Reach Level 3 and charge W into a committed Wukong, then Q3 to lock him before he E's out
edits.after: Reach Level 3, charge W into a committed Wukong, then land the 2-stack Ntofo pull before he dashes

edits.before: Drop the W clone to bait your W charge and Q3, then E-Q in on the real you
